rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers reading the verb as an absolute act of bestowing, with no expressed object.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf evvelkini, İbn Cerîr Taberî ikinciyi tercih etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr Taberî
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers supplying an implicit object, construing the phrase as bestowing something upon them.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf evvelkini, İbn Cerîr Taberî ikinciyi tercih etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı finds the objectless reading safer from ellipsis and rhetorically eloquent, although the second reading is the verb's more apparent construction.
rows.anchor: Haziften selâmet itibariyle evvelkisi evlâ ve beliğ ve fakat bir kinaye mâhiyetindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir uses the following worship covenant to construe the implied object as obedience and worship; Elmalılı instead finds the path itself the more apparent object.
rows.anchor: Ancak İbn Cerîr Taberî bu mef‘ûlü إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ karînesiyle tâat ve ibadete ircâ‘ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı's final reading supplies no pronoun: unrestricted bestowal is a rhetorical indirect expression for bestowing the path.
rows.anchor: Ve en doğrusu burada zamiri takdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This construal makes the path itself a supreme blessing, its bestowal a supreme divine aid, and the path theirs through divine gift and their following it.
rows.anchor: Bunda câlib-i dikkat üç nokta vardır. Evvelâ, bizzat tarîk ve sırâtın ehemm-i ni‘âm olan bir ni‘met-i ‘uzmâ olduğu anlaşılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the route or means to a blessing secures repeated access to it, unlike receiving a single instance of the blessing.
rows.anchor: Çünkü herhangi bir nimetin tarîkine, kanununa nâil olmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for a single benefit is a small request; asking for its path and steadfastness brings it repeatedly, so the opening prayer asks for the straight path.
rows.anchor: burada ibtidâ “bize nimet ver” denmeyip de ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ duasıyla doğru yol istemenin tâlim buyurulması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest path is the route by which divine aid arrives; without God's enabling, even a known and followed route may fail to reach its goal.
rows.anchor: Tarîkin en büyüğü de me‘ûnet-i ilâhiyenin tarîk-i vürûdudur. Bunun en kısası da müstakīm olan tarîktir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a religion and community that carries people through the worship covenant; its beneficiaries are a historically witnessed, successful example, as the next phrase specifies.
rows.anchor: Bu yol إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ahdinde sebat ile yürütecek olan bir din ve millettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipients of blessing are not one bounded historical group but innumerable people and communities appearing across human history under God's nurture.
rows.anchor: İbtidâ-i beşeriyetten bu âna kadar peyderpey gelmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their existence is certain, and asking for their path proceeds from that certainty; their specific members can be identified mentally according to what blessing means.
rows.anchor: Bu nokta yakīnîdir. Ve ‘ale’l-ıtlâk bunların sırâtını talep etmek de bu yakīn ile harekettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an 4:69 names prophets, the truthful, martyrs, the righteous, and their believing companions as the truly blessed; this is the fullest listing, initially viewed from early Islam.
rows.anchor: Kur’an bize bu cinsten birçok cemaatler gösterecektir ki وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Muslims, Muhammad and his Companions form an unambiguous historical example of the blessed community, whose worldly and otherworldly success had no historical parallel.
rows.anchor: Bize gelince; bu numunenin bütün ibhamlarından ârî bir ‘ahd-i hâricîsi vardır ki o da Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ Muhammed Mustafâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar's humble patched garment amid conquests and justice exemplifies the companions' spiritual joy and stature above imperial luxury.
rows.anchor: Ömer’in sırtındaki yamalı bir gömlek âlemin gözüne kisrâların, kayserlerin tâc-ı haşmetlerinden çok yüksek bir hiss-i ibtihâc saçıyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Umar seemed shaken on the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr emerged and guided him and the community back onto Muhammad's path.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Sıddîk bütün sıddîkiyetiyle ibrâz-ı vücûd ederek onu ve herkesi irşad etmiş ve cemaati kemâ fi’s-sâbık sırât-ı Muhammedîde yürütmüştü.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the Hijra cave crisis, Muhammad reassured the grieving Abu Bakr that God was with them, citing Qur'an 9:40.
rows.anchor: diye onu tesliye ve tatmin eden ancak Hazret-i Muhammed olmuş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many earlier and later exegetes explain the path as Muhammad's and his Companions' way and Sunna; considered within the wider class, they remain its exemplary community.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Muhammed’in ve ashâb-ı kirâmının tarîki, sünneti ile tefsir etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the relative phrase qualifies those under wrath and indicates the source of Islam's quality of piety.
rows.anchor: “ٱلَّذِينَ,”غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ’nin sıfatıdır. Ve İslâm’daki haslet-i takvânın menşe’ini gösterir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because adjectives agree with their nouns in definiteness, while gayr is indefinite unless annexed to a complete opposite, the adjective reading signals a mentally specified antecedent.
rows.anchor: Arapça’da sıfat ile mevsuf arasında ta‘rîf veya tenkîr cihetinden dahi mutabakat şarttır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who appear blessed are actually subject to wrath or astray, so gayr excludes these and restricts the blessed to those enjoying sound, safe blessing.
rows.anchor: Mün‘âmun ‘aleyh görünenler içinde hakikatte mahkûm-i gazab veya dâll olan nice kimseler de bulunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If blessing is taken absolutely, gayr cannot be an adjective and may instead be read as a substitute; Elmalılı will reject that analysis in favor of the adjective.
rows.anchor: in‘âm ıtlâkıyla mülâhaza edilir ve الذ�ن de bu sıla ile cinsen veya ‘ahd-i hâricî ile ma‘rife tanılır ise “gayr” ona sıfat olamaz, belki bedel olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf, followed by Qadi and others, allows treating gayr as a substitute; Elmalılı reports Ebussuud's rejection.
rows.anchor: vesâire bu bedeliyeti tecviz etmişlerdir. Fakat Ebussuud tefsirinde bunu bihakkın reddeylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anger is the soul's agitation toward retaliation at something disliked, opposed to satisfaction; Turkish equivalents include anger, indignation, and wrath.
rows.anchor: “Gazab” nefsin bir mekruh karşısında irâde-i intikām ile heyecânıdır ki rızânın zıddıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When attributed to God, anger means its ultimate end, the will to retaliate or impose punishment, and is compatible with merciful lordship: punishing an oppressor serves mercy to the oppressed.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’a nisbet edildiği zaman gazab infi‘âlât-ı nefsâniyeden tecrid ile müntehâ ve gayesinde isti‘mâl edilir de irâde-i intikam veya inzâl-i ukūbet mânası murad olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A temporary punishment or pain that prepares future blessings does not make someone one of those under wrath; outcomes determine the judgment, as 2:155 illustrates.
rows.anchor: وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُم بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْخَوْفِ وَٱلْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَنفُسِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dalaal means straying from the right path, intentionally or accidentally, opposite guidance; it can progress from heedlessness or bewilderment to loss and ruin.
rows.anchor: Dalâl” ve “dalâlet”, doğru yoldan ‘amden veya hatâen sapmaktır ki “hüdâ”nın mukabilidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term first concerns departure from a physical route and extends to mental and spiritual matters; Turkish usage distinguishes religious dalalet from intellectual or verbal sapıklık.
rows.anchor: Esasında mahsüs ve maddî yoldan sapmaktır. Ve sonra ma‘neviyyât ve ma‘kūlâtta da müte‘âref olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite articles in the wrath and deviation phrases most naturally mark generic, comprehensive categories, excluding every unbelieving path from the fully safe blessing.
rows.anchor: Burada gerek ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ ve gerek ٱلضَّآلِّينَ’deki harf-i ta‘rîflerin istiğrak veya cins için olduğu zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the definite articles may refer to the earliest external examples; excluding even their minimum certain cases rhetorically entails avoiding all worse cases.
rows.anchor: harf-i ta‘rîflerin akdem olan ‘ahd-i hâricî mânasına hamllerinde dahi aynı mânayı dolayısıyla istihsâl mümkindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an also attributes divine wrath to disbelievers generally and describes those who reject God's way as far astray, supporting the comprehensive reading.
rows.anchor: وَلَٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًۭا فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an explicitly says that those who disbelieve and obstruct God's way have gone far astray, extending the category beyond specific communities.
rows.anchor: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ قَدْ ضَلُّوا۟ ضَلَٰلًۢا بَعِيدًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran associates Jews with wrath and Christians with deviation, citing 2:61 for Jews; 5:77 separately identifies Christians with deviation.
rows.anchor: Yehûd hakkında ekseriya وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran describes Christians as having strayed from the right way, citing 5:77.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ hakkında da قُلْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَا تَغْلُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ ٱلْحَقِّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews and Christians remain distinguishable from other unbelievers in close dealings, such as permission to eat their slaughter and marry their daughters, and are Islam's nearest opposite.
rows.anchor: Yehûd ile Nasârâ’nın kestiklerini yemek ve kızlarını nikâh edebilmek gibi yakın mu‘âmelâtta diğer ehl-i şirkten farklarını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim, as quoted by al-Durr al-Manthur, says he knows of no exegetical disagreement identifying those under wrath as Jews and those astray as Christians.
rows.anchor: demiştir ki: “‘Mağdûbun ‘aleyhim’in Yehûd ve ‘dâllîn’in Nasârâ ile tefsîrinde beyne’l-müfessirîn hilâf bilmiyorum.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Hibban and Hakim judged the relevant reports sound, Tirmidhi judged them fair, and many hadith scholars transmitted them.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî de hüsnüne hükmetmiş ve bunları birçok muhaddisîn tahric eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes object that restricting the Qur'anic wording to two groups would violate its generality, and prefer treating Jews and Christians as examples.
rows.anchor: bazı müfessirîn buna ilişmiş ve nassın umûmiyet üzere ibkāsıyla Yehûd ve Nasârâ’yı birer misâl olarak telakkī etmeyi muvâfık görmüştür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı accepts the external-reference reading only if Jews and Christians are minimum certain examples, so exclusion of them implies exclusion of all others; limiting the verse to them alone contradicts reason and decisive reports.
rows.anchor: bunlar ednâ-yı müteyakkan olarak tasavvur edilirse diğerlerinden ihtirâz-ı ‘âm bi’l-evleviyye sâbit olacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worship covenant already clearly excludes polytheists, while this verse explicitly excludes Jews and Christians and implicitly excludes the others, a rhetorically apt distinction.
rows.anchor: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ’de şirkleri zâhir olan müşrikîn-i sâireden vâzıhan

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites a hadith that Tirmidhi grades hasan, transmitted from Adi b. Hatim, in which the Prophet says Jews are under wrath and Christians are astray.
rows.anchor: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz’in “Yehûd mağdûbun ‘aleyhim, Nasârâ da dullâldir” buyurduğunu Tirmizî Sahîh’inin

rows.speaker: Adî b. Hâtim
rows.claim: Adi recounts that the Prophet welcomed him, took his hand, helped a woman and child with their need, then spoke with him about faith; Adi subsequently professed Islam.
rows.anchor: Cemaat ‘İşte bu Adî b. Hâtim’dir’ dediler. Ben ise emansız, mükâtebesiz gelmiştim

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet warns listeners to give charity, however little, as protection from Hell; at judgment God will ask what they prepared from the gifts they received.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah kalktı, namaz kıldı, ba‘dehu onları tergībe başladı. Diyordu ki: ‘Velev bir sâ‘, velev yarım sâ‘

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet says that if a person cannot give even half a date, a kind word can serve as protection; he reassures the audience that God's help removes fear of poverty.
rows.anchor: Her biriniz Allah’a varacak, O da ona şu söyleyeceğimi söyleyecektir: «Ben size göz kulak vermedim mi?»

rows.speaker: Adî b. Hâtim
rows.claim: Adi recalls thinking about how the Prophet's assurances compared with the bandits of the Tay mountains.
rows.anchor: Adî b. Hâtim hazretleri bunu rivayet ettikten sonra şunu da ilâve etmiş: “Bunu dinlerken ben gönlümden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that Jews are among those under wrath is not equivalent to saying that all those under wrath are Jews; the hadiths make them examples, not the exhaustive referent.
rows.anchor: Fakat “Yehûd mağdûbun ‘aleyhimdir” deme kle “el-mağdûbi ‘aleyhim Yehûd’dur” demek arasında büyük fark vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because an external-reference reading is plausible without restricting the Qur'an to non-mutawatir reports, both interpretations of the hadiths should be applied; the external reading implies comprehensive exclusion.
rows.anchor: takyîd-i nas mahzûru vârid olmayacağı cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic reading excludes all others explicitly, while the external-reference reading excludes other unbelievers implicitly; Elmalılı finds the latter more consistent with the Qur'anic context because it distinguishes polytheists from People of the Book.
rows.anchor: ikincide ise bu fark dahi gösterilmiş olur ki biz bunu siyâk-ı Kur’ân’a daha muvâfık buluyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Christians then ruled major powers and could appear blessed, Elmalılı says their true condition and afterlife were perilous.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ’ya gelince; o zaman bunlar Roma’nın vârisi, İstanbul’un sâhibi olarak yer yüzündeki iki büyük devletin biri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christianity abandoned divine unity for the Trinity and idols, though its recognition of a Father-God retained a limited unitarian element compared with Manichaeans and Zoroastrians.
rows.anchor: Evvelemirde tevhîd-i Hakk’a bedel ‘akīde-i teslîse saplanmışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its doctrine made God both one and three through the union of three persons, violating the law of noncontradiction and stunting intellectual development.
rows.anchor: hem bir, hem üç idi. Böyle aklın tenakuz kanununu da çiğneyen bir ‘akīde-i teslîs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Christians derailed inherited sciences and abandoned proof for emotional inclination, using psychology and popular sentiment to influence ordinary people and rationalize excess.
rows.anchor: vâris oldukları bütün ulûm u fünûnu çığırından çıkarmış ve tarîk-i isbâttan ayrılıp sadece zevk-i kalbîye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christian legal thought severed right and law from truth, treating law neither as divine or scientific nor as dependent on the people's will.
rows.anchor: Nazarlarında hak, şeriat mefhûmunun hakikatle alakası yoktu; bunlar ilmî, hakīkī ve ilâhî bir mefhum değil idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clergy and councils made law by will rather than knowledge or interpretation, allowing arbitrary rules and joining divine and human realms incoherently.
rows.anchor: vaz‘ı idi. Ve bunlar hak üzerinde bir fikr-i ilmî ve ictihâdî ile değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This arbitrary law denied non-Christians a right to live, undermined social order, and eventually collapsed because emotional pleasures cannot sustain injustice to human rights.
rows.anchor: Hıristiyanlardan mâ‘adâsına hiçbir suretle hakk-ı hayat tanımaması hey’et-i ictimâ‘iyeyi büyük sukūtlara ihzar ediyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı sets aside sins not arising from doctrine, distinguishing personal misconduct from the religious traits under discussion.
rows.anchor: Burada akideden neş’et etmeyen ve akide hilâfında vâki‘olan fısk u fücûrdan bahse lüzum görmüyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defining Christian traits he lists amount to departure from the prophetic truth, whose consequence is punishment and misguidance despite outward worldly prosperity.
rows.anchor: teslis, ta‘kīm-i ‘ukūl, sayd-ı kulûb, şeriatsızlık, vicdan darlığı ve hâsılı bir kelime ile hakk u hakikatten tebâ‘üd

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Muslims Islam as a safe path to complete blessing; its rapid early success established the promise, and those steadfast on it will have the same outcome eternally.
rows.anchor: pek az bir zaman içinde de bununla tedeyyün edenlere vaad ve in‘âm-ı ilâhî şekk ü şüpheden âzâde olarak tahakkuk etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha's opening treats knowledge of God, its middle establishes divine relation and social and legal principles, and its last three verses define Islam's path with comprehensive eloquence.
rows.anchor: üç âyette de tarîk-i hakkın, dîn-i İslâm’ın efrâdını câmi‘, ağyârını mâni‘bir hadd-i tâmmını tasvîrine doyulmaz bir belâgat ile tesbit etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam is the clear, straight, safe road that leads to God and His blessings without wrath or misguidance, followed by people historically witnessed to attain true happiness and gratitude.
rows.anchor: Gazaba uğratmadan, dalâlete düşürmeden doğruca ve selâmetle Allah’a ve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious practice begins by knowing God and making a fully monotheistic covenant, then asking for guidance to a straight divine law that teaches duties and enables their steadfast practice.
rows.anchor: Bu din ile tedeyyünün, diyânetin mebde’i evvelâ Allah teâlâ’yı tanımak ve O’na إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings make the request and practice; God gives religion, law, and two forms of guidance: intellectual instruction from the Qur'an and practical enabling through accepting it.
rows.anchor: taleb ve diyânet bizden; din, şeriat, hidâyet Allah’tandır ve bu hidâyet iki nevidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha substantiates Islam through observation, experience, and historical testimony after its rational and spiritual guidance, requiring no further proof.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha bunu târif ederken mazmûnunu isbat için bidâyetteki irşâdât-ı akliye ve kalbiyeden sonra müşahede ve tecribeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his Companions provide a visible historical example of the greatness and sanctity of divine blessings attained through Islam.
rows.anchor: Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Muhammed Mustafâ sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Efendimiz’le ashâb-ı kirâmının bu sâyede mazhar oldukları ni‘am-ı ilâhiyenin azamet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Qur'an is preserved letter for letter and Prophetic practice is preserved, Islam has suffered no deviation; the Qur'an is Muhammad's clearest miracle and history testifies to his truth.
rows.anchor: kitâb-ı ilâhî bir harfine bile halel gelmeksizin aynen mevcut ve sünen-i nebeviye mahfuz olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious knowledge joins reason and transmitted tradition; societies that apply it sincerely can expect the same results confirmed by experience, and denying this is to reject induction.
rows.anchor: bizim için ilm-i dîn akıl ve nakil ile memzucdur. Bunları sıdk u ihlâs ile tatbik edecek olan hey’et-i ictimâ‘iyelerin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Europeans mislead inquiry by testing Islam among currently declining Muslims instead of investigating its genuine sources and comparing present practice with past practice.
rows.anchor: şimdiki inhitat içinde yuvarlanan Müslümanlarda arıyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who genuinely follow the straight path advance, while those who do not decline; the divine law is true even when religious practice is incomplete or insincere.
rows.anchor: Demek ki sâdıklar müterakkī, gayr-i sâdıklar mütedennîdirler. Demek ki din kānûn-ı hak lâkin diyânet nâtamam ve gayr-i sâdıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to apply arithmetic or hygiene does not discredit those sciences; likewise, people are responsible for conforming to true law rather than bending it to themselves.
rows.anchor: İnsanlar kendilerini kānûn-ı hakka uydurmakla mükellef iken o kānûn-ı hakkı kendilerine uydurmaya çalışırlarsa kusur o kanunun değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who knowingly disobey incur divine wrath, while the unwitting are misguided and ultimately face the same consequence.
rows.anchor: Gazab-ı ilâhî evvelâ bunu bilerek yapanlar içindir. Bilmeyerek yapanlar da dâllîndirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern people seek to fit true law to themselves, causing human distress to grow despite advances in science; only following the right path can end that distress.
rows.anchor: bütün âlemde ıztırâbât-ı beşeriyenin sûret-i umûmiyede gittikçe artmasının sebebi de budur. Bu ıztırabâtı ancak tarîk-i hakka sülûk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin is an imperative-like noun of action meaning 'answer' or 'accept'; it is not part of Qur'anic wording and therefore is not written in the codex.
rows.anchor: “Âmin” icâbet et, kabul et mânasına bir ism-i fiildir. “Âmin” demeye de “te’mîn” denilir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A Bukhari and Muslim hadith instructs everyone to say amin when the imam says waladdallin; agreement with the angels' amin brings forgiveness of past sins.
rows.anchor: İmam ‘veleddâllîn’ dediği zaman hepiniz ‘âmin’ deyiniz. Çünkü melekler ‘âmin’ derler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separate suspended report says the ranks of the people on earth align with the heavenly ranks, and earthly amin coinciding with heavenly amin brings forgiveness.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i arzın saflarını ehl-i semânın safları vely eder. Binâen‘aleyh yerdeki ‘âmin’ gökteki ‘âmîn’e tevâfuk ederse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin is established by Sunna and should be said quietly by the imam, congregation, and a person praying alone.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh âmin sünnet ile sâbittir. Hem imam ve hem cemaat tarafından sırren yapılmalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the command as glorifying the name of one's Lord, the Most High.
rows.anchor: Meâl: Tesbih et Rabbinin a‘lâ ismine
